title: AWS Well-Architected Framework
description: Learn the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework and how to apply them.

data.text: The AWS Well-Architected Framework is a set of best practices and guidelines for building secure, high-performing, resilient, and efficient cloud systems. It helps you understand the pros and cons of architectural decisions and provides a consistent approach to evaluating your workloads.

data.title: Built on Six Pillars
data.text: The Framework is organized around six pillars. Each pillar represents a core area of cloud architecture. Together they form a comprehensive checklist for building great systems on AWS.

rows: Running and monitoring systems, improving processes
How do you run and monitor your workload to deliver business value?
How do you protect your information, systems, and assets?
How do you ensure your workload can recover from failures?
How do you use computing resources efficiently to meet requirements?
How do you avoid or eliminate costs?
How do you minimize the environmental impact of running cloud workloads?

data.text: Operational excellence focuses on operations, observability, and continuous improvement. Security emphasizes protecting data and systems. Reliability covers the ability to recover from failures. Performance efficiency is about using resources effectively. Cost optimization helps you spend only what you need. Sustainability addresses the environmental impact of your workloads.

terms.definition: An AWS set of best practices for building secure, reliable, and efficient cloud systems.
One of the six core areas of the Framework, such as security or cost optimization.
The pillar focused on running and monitoring workloads, and improving processes.
The newest pillar focused on reducing the environmental impact of cloud workloads.

data.title: Applying the Framework
data.content: When launching a new web application, the Well-Architected Framework helps you ask the right questions. For security, you might ask: Are we encrypting data at rest and in transit? For reliability: Can the application survive the failure of one server? For cost: Are we using the right instance types for our workload?
data.code:
# Use the AWS Well-Architected Tool to review your workload
aws wellarchitected get-review-report \
  --workload-id a1b2c3d4-5678-90ab-cdef-EXAMPLE11111 \
  --milestone-number 1 \
  --output text

data.title: How to Use the Framework
items: Review each pillar against your current workload.
Identify areas where you can improve.
Use the AWS Well-Architected Tool in the console for automated checks.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: The Well-Architected Framework has six pillars covering operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability
It provides a structured way to evaluate and improve your AWS workloads
The Framework is applicable to any workload regardless of industry or size
AWS provides a free tool to help you assess your architecture against the pillars
data.takeaway: You now understand the foundation of AWS. Next, you will dive into how to secure your account with Identity and Access Management.
